project.title: Software Based Model Development for Design of Area Specific Shelter for Thermal Comfort Maintenance

weather.handling: Hourly NASA forcing held constant over six 10-minute thermal substeps; solar position recomputed at each substep midpoint.

model.class: physics-based reduced-order transient thermal screening model
model.topology: one indoor air node + one 2R1C thermal-mass node per opaque facade/roof/exposed-floor surface

solar.transposition: direct beam + isotropic diffuse + ground reflected
solar.windowSolarTreatment: SHGC * area * surface irradiance, added to zone

model.infiltration: constant ACH with dry-air density from PSC pressure and outdoor temperature

headlineHeatFlow72h.basis: ideal-heating mode at 20 C; cumulative Jan 15-17

explanation: Modest insulation leaves conductive losses high during the severe winter window.
1.50 ACH produces the largest cold-air replacement loss of the three cases.
The 2.40 m² primary glazing faces east, limiting midday winter solar access.

headlineHeatFlow72h.basis: ideal-heating mode at 20 C; cumulative Jan 15-17

explanation: More insulation sharply reduces wall, roof and raised-floor heat loss.
Lower window U-value cuts glazing conduction while total glazing stays 3.00 m².
Reducing infiltration from 1.50 to 0.70 ACH materially lowers air-leakage heat loss.

explanation: The strongest envelope and 0.40 ACH produce the lowest auxiliary-heating burden.
The same 2.40 m² primary glazing is rotated south rather than enlarged.
South-facing winter solar access increases useful glazing gain during daylight hours.

orientationOnlyDiagnostic.method: counterfactual diagnostic only: Scenario 03 envelope, U/SHGC, ACH and 3.00 m2 glazing held fixed; primary facade east vs south

modelDisclosure: Physics-based reduced-order thermal screening model. Results are comparative engineering estimates and depend on weather, material, leakage and boundary-condition assumptions. The prototype demonstrates a planned simulation workflow using precomputed results; it is not a live CFD/FEM/digital-twin or certified comfort model.

sanityChecks.heatFlowSignConvention: positive = heat entering indoor zone; losses reported as positive magnitudes of negative zone exchange

calculationNotes.sourceConflictResolution: The older report's centered-mass opaque-solar source was not used because it failed the high-insulation physics sanity check; the prior Admin brief's exterior sol-air boundary treatment was used instead. This prevents absorbed exterior solar from bypassing half the insulation in the 2R1C reduction.
calculationNotes.pressureChoice: The raw file contains both PS (MERRA-2 grid-cell surface pressure, grid elevation 4532.61 m) and PSC (pressure corrected by NASA for the requested 3500 m site elevation). PSC is used in air-density calculations.
